items.title: 5 robbery suspects collared by cops on major road in Mississauga
items.summary: A robbery near Niagara Falls on Sunday afternoon was followed by the arrest of five suspects just over an hour later on a major road in Mississauga, police say. m. at a business on Vansickle Road in St. Catharines. Police didn’t specify what type of business was targeted. Moments earlier, according to investigators, five males had pulled up to the shop in a stolen car, forced their way inside the business and stole an unspecified number of cellphones before quickly fleeing the scene. Criminal Investigations Bureau officers with Niagara police took over the probe and set about tracking the suspects. , Ontario Provincial Police arrested five suspects on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga, about a 45-minute drive from the crime scene. Police said the stolen vehicle and merchandise were recovered. Investigators didn’t provide details about the arrest of the suspects, nor did they say where the car had been stolen from.

items.title: Costco and Metro Carry This Mississauga Chocolate Brand, Now Squeezed by a 50 Percent U.S. Ingredient Tariff
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, ZoRaw Chocolates, a Mississauga based chocolate maker, is facing higher costs after Canada's 50 per cent counter-tariff hit one of its core U.S. sourced ingredients. The outlet reports the five year old company produces 30,000 low-sugar, high-protein chocolate bars daily, relying heavily on cacao and whey protein isolate. ZoRaw's products already sit on shelves in nearly 4,000 Canadian retail stores, including Costco and Metro, and Walmart and Loblaws are expected to carry them soon, Mississauga.com said. The company noted it had spent years customizing its relationship with its American supplier before the tariff took effect. The outlet said the case reflects the wider strain Canada's trade dispute with the United States is placing on local manufacturers that depend on U.S. sourced ingredients.

items.title: Mississauga's Polish Community Pushed This Toronto Film Festival to Finally Add Local Screenings
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the 17th annual Ekran Toronto Polish Film Festival runs from Nov. 18 to 29 this year, with screenings returning for a second year to venues in Toronto, Mississauga and Hamilton. The outlet reports founder and executive director Marta Pozniakowski had for years heard audience members ask for screenings closer to where they actually live. Census data cited by Mississauga.com shows Mississauga has more than 22,000 Polish speaking residents and over 36,000 people who identify as ethnically Polish. The festival expanded beyond its traditional base in Toronto's Roncesvalles neighbourhood in 2025, adding Mississauga and Hamilton to its main lineup after years of one-off screenings in those cities. Mississauga.com notes organizers made the change specifically to meet a Polish Canadian audience that now stretches well beyond west-end Toronto.

items.title: Warm up this winter with City programs and March Break camps
items.summary: Discover a range of sports, arts and culture programs to keep you moving this winter. Winter is a great time to learn something new, stay active and connect with your community. The City of Mississauga is offering a wide range of March Break camps and recreation and culture programs for residents of all ages, interests and abilities. From swimming and skating lessons and fitness classes to sports, photography, fine arts, drama and dance programs, there are many opportunities to build skills, explore new interests and stay engaged all season long. Residents can begin browsing and bookmarking programs on Active Mississauga starting November 17. Creating a wish list ahead of registration helps act faster when signing up for popular programs that fill up quickly. Registration opens on November 24 for Mississauga residents and December 1 for non-residents. The City of Mississauga provides programs in safe, inclusive and welcoming spaces for all ages and abilities, and supporting different interests, skill levels and accessibility needs. People of all ages and abilities, ranging from preschool-aged children to older adults. Registration for winter recreation and culture programs and March Break camps. The programs are delivered by qualified staff, with children’s programs guided by HIGH FIVE® quality standards to help ensure positive recreation experiences for participants and families. Browse programs, create wish lists and register through Active Mississauga. In-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours. Whether you’re introducing your child to water, building confidence as a swimmer or pursuing aquatic leadership certifications, the City offers swimming programs for all ages and skill levels.

Alvin Tedjo toppled two political veterans in a hard-fought Mississauga mayoral election, and one of the key promises that helped propel him to victory was a two-year property tax freeze for all residents. At Mississauga’s inaugural council meeting on Monday night, Tedjo made it clear that he intends to keep that promise. “In my first act as Mayor, I am issuing a Mayoral Directive to city staff to officially begin the work to achieve a 0 per cent tax increase in the forthcoming 2027 budget, and the 2028 budget,” Tedjo said in his first address to council after swearing-in ceremonies concluded.

items.title: Officer worried about ‘ambush’ during fatal shooting on Mississauga man, inquest hears
items.summary: A police constable told a coroner’s inquest Monday he was concerned about the risk of an ambush as he approached a car that had crashed into a pillar after it was hit by police gunfire during a botched arrest in Mississauga nearly seven years ago. It was dark at the time and the car’s windows were heavily tinted, making it difficult to see inside, Peel Regional Police Const. Marc Charlebois, then a member of the force’s tactical unit, told the inquest into the death of Jamal Francique. m. on Jan. 7, 2020, and arrived at the townhouse complex about 20 minutes later, he said. As he came up toward the back of the car, carrying a ballistic shield more than a metre long and a metal bar designed for breaking or prying into windows, the officer said he and a colleague called out some commands, but there was no answer. Charlebois, who is the first witness in the inquest, said he managed to see the lone person in the car after breaking the rear passenger window. “I can just see the back of his right side, the right side of his head. … I can hear the male struggling for breath,” he said. Charlebois saw blood, he said, but didn’t yet realize Francique had a gunshot wound. There was no sign of movement, he said. ” inquest counsel Roger Shallow asked the constable.

items.title: OPP Says Driver Ramped Onto Tow Truck Deck Before Rollover Crash Near Mississauga's Dixie Road
items.summary: According to the OPP Highway Safety Division, a tow truck operator was struck and seriously injured on Highway 401 near Dixie Road on Sunday while assisting a disabled driver. Police say a third vehicle struck the tilt and lift tow truck, ramped onto its deck, hit the vehicle being loaded, and then rolled over. The tow truck operator was also struck and was rushed to hospital with serious, non-life-threatening injuries, police said. The OPP noted that starting Jan. 1, Ontario's move over rules will expand to cover certain stopped work vehicles with flashing amber lights, including Ministry of Transportation vehicles. Police said failing to slow down, move over or let an emergency vehicle pass can bring fines of 400 to 2,000 dollars, three demerit points and a licence suspension of up to two years.
